reason: Not refuted as a zero-cost calibration item: text only, no submission, no kernel, never a finals input (finals ticked 09:10Z [56563521, 56563534]); fits R1-R10 and needs no user OK beyond the usual commit. Its value is the lessons read only (score gain 0, stated honestly), and it is incremental: round9/LESSONS_draft.md s5 already has the PRIVATE table (#37, #38, #34) and the question 'K2 - twin on private?'. What it adds is numeric predictions written before the reveal, plus the free controls #35 56545786 and P36. Three claims need fixing. (1) 'Our private position vs the 0.953 block depends only on sign(private(K2) - private(x138))' is wrong. Our private score is max(#37, #38), and the twin is not byte-identical to x138 (lowrefine readmits nodes). The 345-team block is not all x138 copies. Each rival's private is the max of its own two selected (or auto-selected) subs. So a rank-vs-block read is confounded; use per-submission private scores. (2) P2 (displayed private K2 > #34 strictly, P~0.75) is overconfident. Scores are read at 3 decimals (poll.log/ledger), the expected effect is ~+0.001, and the transfer is 0..0.3 of the lab size (LESSONS s1). So P(displayed diff >= +0.001) is ~0.5-0.6, and ties must be defined. (3) P1's '(>= 0) P~0.8' needs an exact event definition.
